PullRequest.Title: Refactoring prompts for openAI models
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request updates the Copilot extension to replace references to HiddenModel N with GPT-6, ensuring proper capability detection and prompt routing for the new model. Key changes include:

- Introduced `isGpt6Family` to identify GPT-6 models using `family.startsWith('gpt-6')`.
- Renamed the prompt file to `gpt6Prompt.tsx` and updated related capabilities, patch instructions, and todo-tool descriptions.
- Removed all references to HiddenModel N while maintaining existing functionality for other models.
- Added new tests for the changes and ensured that all existing tests passed successfully.

Validation has been performed with 104 tests passing, and ESLint checks have been completed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or continue an agent chat using a GPT-6 family endpoint, including prompt selection, tool filtering, request-body construction, and optional tool search.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PromptRegistry scans its bounded resolver list, performs an O(family-length) prefix check, renders the selected static prompt bundle, filters available tools, and constructs the model request before the network completion can begin. If the model requests a deferred tool, embedding search and the follow-up model turn are then on the critical path; otherwise that work is absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sends the normal streamed Responses API model request, with GPT-6 prompt-cache, verbosity, and deferred-tool metadata selected by the changed capability predicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model request per agent turn, unchanged; prompt-cache metadata adds only bounded fields. The initial tool schema set can shrink because deferred tools are omitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request boundary already existed. The hidden-model family used equivalent capability gates; externally named GPT-6 families previously fell through to generic routing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is the main agent-turn critical path. The diff changes bounded request metadata and prompt/tool selection, not the number of ordinary completion requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Computes one query embedding and, on a cold tool cache, one batched set of embeddings for missing deferred tools before local ranking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero unless the model emits a tool-search call; then one query embedding per call and at most one batched missing-tool computation for the effective deferred-tool set. Existing prompt instructions explicitly discourage repeated searches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Named GPT-6 families were not selected by the old hidden hash predicate, so fallback capability inference did not enable this protocol unless metadata explicitly did. The prior hidden-model aliases already used this same tool-search path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When invoked, embedding search blocks returning selected tool definitions and therefore the next model turn. When no deferred tool is needed, it is off the critical path and deferred tool schemas are omitted from the initial request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continues the agent with selected deferred tool definitions after a model-requested tool search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one additional model round trip per emitted tool-search call; not per available tool, because selected definitions are returned together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing protocol applied to hidden-model aliases and other supported families; named GPT-6 fallback routing did not infer support before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a round trip only when GPT-6 asks to load a deferred tool, while reducing ordinary request serialization and token payload by omitting all deferred schemas.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resolver count and enabled-tool count per request; deferred-tool search scales with the number of deferred tools after non-deferred filtering, and returns five matches by default. There is no new per-file, per-message, or unbounded concurrent loop in the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resolver matching is sequential over a small registry as before. Tool definitions are processed synchronously once per request. A requested tool search performs one query-embedding operation, batches embeddings for cache-missing tool definitions, ranks locally, then continues the existing serialized agent turn; the diff adds no parallel burst or limiter bypass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The removed hidden-family predicate used a cached SHA-256 lookup; the replacement prefix comparison requires no cache and is cheaper on cold and warm paths. Tool definition embeddings use precomputed and local caches plus an in-memory promise map; a cold search may batch missing tool embeddings, while warm searches reuse tool embeddings but still compute one query embedding. GPT-6 prompt cache-breakpoint metadata uses the existing conversation cache behavior and does not add a local retained collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and cardinality: changed GPT-6 capability checks feed endpoint.supportsToolSearch, agent tool selection, prompt rendering, and Responses API deferral. High confidence that no accidental fan-out or new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual deferred-tool counts, embedding backend latency, model tool-search frequency, and provider metadata overrides vary by installation. The mechanism is bounded and intentionally trades an occasional search round trip for smaller ordinary prompts; there is no evidence that the changed family routing produces a net regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The route change enables the existing GPT-6-specific protocol and static prompt bundle; ordinary turns avoid deferred schemas, while optional search work is model-triggered, grouped, cached, and serialized.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attach one or more PDF documents to a GPT-6 chat request.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each explicitly attached PDF, FileVariable checks vision/PDF support, reads the file, validates four magic bytes, base64-encodes the complete buffer, and embeds it in the user message before the model network request can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads the complete attached PDF from the workspace file service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per explicitly attached PDF per render; scales with attachment count and file size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A named GPT-6 family not otherwise identified as GPT-5-plus was treated as not PDF-capable and omitted the attachment; hidden-model aliases already reached the same read path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read must complete before prompt construction and the network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copies the PDF buffer into a base64 string and includes it in the request payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-file encoding per accepted attachment, with output proportional to total PDF bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Named GPT-6 fallback routing omitted unsupported PDF content, whereas the prior hidden GPT-6 aliases performed the same native-PDF serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Encoding and request-byte growth occur before and during the model request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: agent chat endpoint request with Document content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Uploads base64 PDF document parts in the model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One chat request containing all accepted attachments; bytes scale with aggregate PDF size rather than producing one network call per PDF.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The public GPT-6 family was not inferred as PDF-capable before the change; hidden aliases already supported the same upload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Upload size can increase request latency, but it is the requested native-PDF feature.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and byte size of explicitly attached PDFs. Effective cardinality is one filesystem read and one base64 allocation per attachment; no deduplication or cache exists in this component.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each FileVariable render awaits its file read. Overall prompt-render scheduling is outside the changed code; this diff adds no Promise.all, queue, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no PDF-content cache here, so repeated prompt renders can reread and re-encode attachments. That behavior already applied to model families classified as PDF-capable, including the prior hidden-model aliases; the diff only recognizes the public GPT-6 family name.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the family predicate enables the existing filesystem read and full-buffer serialization for named GPT-6 endpoints.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PDF size and attachment count vary, but the resource mechanism is explicit and proportional to user-selected content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added work is the direct, necessary implementation of intentionally enabling native PDF attachments for GPT-6, is triggered only by explicit attachments, and does not introduce accidental repetition or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare edit and notebook tools plus model-specific todo/apply-patch descriptions for a GPT-6 agent request.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Capability checks select apply_patch exclusively, optionally substitute its shorter schema/instructions, choose notebook representation, and shallow-copy the todo definition during the existing enabled-tool scan before request serialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Selects the notebook representation later serialized into agent context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One representation choice per notebook conversion; serialization scales with cells and content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Named GPT-6 families already matched the generic GPT branch and used JSON notebook representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notebook serialization can be on prompt construction's critical path, but the changed GPT-6 predicate does not alter it because the pre-existing generic `family.startsWith('gpt')` branch already selected JSON.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: agent request carrying filtered edit tools and todo definition
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes the selected tool schemas and prompt instructions into the existing model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request payload per turn; the GPT-6 path removes the generic edit_file tool when apply_patch is available and can use shorter apply-patch instructions, while replacing one short todo description with another bounded description.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The model request already serialized enabled tools. Hidden aliases had equivalent overrides; named GPT-6 used generic GPT apply-patch support but retained additional edit tooling and instructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional boundary call is introduced; payload size is bounded and is likely reduced by exclusive/simplified apply_patch selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled-tool count and notebook cell/content size. The todo override is one bounded shallow copy; tool filtering remains one pass over enabled tools. Notebook conversion scales with notebook content, but GPT-prefixed families already selected JSON before this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All changed checks and definition substitutions are synchronous. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or extra network operation is launched by these predicates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration/experiment lookups use existing services. No new cache, retained key, or invalidation path is added. Prompt and tool definitions are reconstructed on the existing per-request path as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed predicates and their direct consumers that all work is bounded per request and no expensive boundary is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token savings depend on enabled tools and experiment state, but there is no scaling-cost increase attributable to the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changes are constant-time classification and bounded metadata substitutions; existing notebook serialization behavior is unchanged and edit-tool payloads generally become smaller.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the extension module and register agent prompt resolvers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At extension startup, allAgentPrompts imports one renamed module and PromptRegistry appends one resolver, exactly as before.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed module and resolver count; independent of workspace size, history, files, or requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module loading and registration as before; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem scan, database call, or network request is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lifecycle changes. The old hidden-model hash list is removed; runtime classification no longer depends on the SHA cache for this family.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the one-for-one import rename and one-for-one registry registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; import and registration shape is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup regression: module count, prompt class size, and registration cardinality are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 9 changed files and every diff page. Traced prompt routing, endpoint capability setup, tool filtering/deferral, embedding search, PDF attachment I/O and encoding, notebook formatting, request serialization, and startup registration. The PR replaces cached hash classification with a cheaper prefix check and extends existing bounded GPT-6 behavior; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
